product.name: RailSecure ETCS Level 2 Onboard Unit
product.description: European Train Control System (ETCS) Level 2 onboard unit for main-line railway operations. Implements Subset-026 v3.6.0 baseline movement authority, speed supervision, and cab signalling. Communicates with Radio Block Centre via GSM-R and 4G fallback. Safety-critical software classified SIL-4 under EN 50128.
product.intended_use: Safe movement authority management and speed supervision for main-line and high-speed rail. Intended for use by licensed train operators across the EU rail network. Must be operated only within homologated infrastructure environments certified per EN 50159.

releases.release_notes: Initial market release. Baseline ETCS L2 Subset-026 v3.4.0 implementation with GSM-R radio interface. Homologated for DB Netz, RFI, and SNCF infrastructure.

vulnerability_reports.title: GSM-R Radio Link Authentication Bypass (Pre-Shared Key Weakness)
vulnerability_reports.description: The GSM-R radio link management module accepts bearer tokens generated with a static pre-shared key embedded in firmware. An attacker with access to base station infrastructure or a rogue BTS can forge valid movement authority acknowledgements, potentially allowing train control commands to appear authenticated when they are not. CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H scored 8.7.

vulnerability_reports.title: Balise Telegram Parser Stack Overflow via Malformed NID_PACKET
vulnerability_reports.description: A stack-allocated buffer in the Eurobalise telegram parser does not validate the NID_PACKET field length against a fixed 512-byte boundary before performing memcpy. A malformed balise transponder in the track can trigger a stack overflow, corrupting the call stack of the safety-critical supervision task. Independently discovered by two research teams.

security_advisories.title: GSM-R Authentication Bypass — Mandatory Firmware Update
security_advisories.summary: A vulnerability in the GSM-R radio link authentication module allows a sophisticated attacker with physical proximity to rail infrastructure to forge movement authority acknowledgements. Operators must apply firmware patch 3.1.5-SEC immediately and report completion to their NoBo.
security_advisories.workaround: Restrict train operations to infrastructure with physical security perimeter around all GSM-R base stations. Increase manual lookout frequency. Report any anomalous radio behaviour to operations centre immediately.
security_advisories.remediation_steps: 1. Schedule maintenance window. 2. Apply firmware 3.1.5-SEC via certified field service engineer. 3. Verify installation via diagnostic tool RS-DIAG v2.3+. 4. Update homologation records with your NoBo. 5. Confirm completion to RailSecure support within 30 days.

security_updates.title: 3.1.5-SEC: GSM-R Authentication Hardening Patch
security_updates.description: Replaces the static pre-shared key scheme with HMAC-SHA256 challenge-response derived from per-unit keys provisioned during manufacturing. Requires key injection via RS-KEYMGR v1.4 tool during field installation. Backward compatible with existing infrastructure.
security_updates.integrity_info: SHA-256: e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855 (firmware image). Signed with RailSecure Code Signing CA G2, cert serial 0x4A3F.

security_updates.title: 3.1.6-SEC: Balise Parser Bounds Check Fix
security_updates.description: Adds explicit length validation of NID_PACKET prior to all telegram buffer operations. Replaces stack-allocated parse buffer with heap allocation with guard pages. Fuzz-tested against 10 million synthetic malformed balise telegrams per EN 50128 test requirements.
security_updates.integrity_info: SHA-256: a665a45920422f9d417e4867efdc4fb8a04a1f3fff1fa07e998e86f7f7a27ae3. RailSecure Code Signing CA G2.

sbom_records.notes: Generated during final integration build. Covers all statically linked libraries. Dynamic OS kernel components documented separately in technical file.

releases.release_notes: Substantial modification: added 4G LTE fallback radio interface and updated Subset-026 baseline to v3.6.0. New conformity assessment conducted by TÜV SÜD Rail. Addresses all known security issues in 3.1.x branch. Introduces ETCS Application Level 3 readiness module (disabled by default, homologation pending).

vulnerability_reports.title: 4G LTE Module: TLS 1.2 Downgrade via Renegotiation Attack
vulnerability_reports.description: The 4G LTE communication module uses mbedTLS 3.1.0 which is vulnerable to renegotiation-based downgrade attacks when MBEDTLS_SSL_RENEGOTIATION is enabled. An on-path attacker controlling 4G infrastructure could force cipher suite negotiation to RC4, enabling session decryption. Reported via coordinated disclosure.

vulnerability_reports.title: Diagnostic Interface: Unauthenticated Command Execution via Serial Port
vulnerability_reports.description: The RS-232 diagnostic interface accepts firmware update commands without any authentication if the physical diagnostic connector is accessible. While requiring physical access, train maintenance facilities may have shared access among contractors. Classified medium due to physical access requirement but elevated in railway context given supply chain risks.

security_advisories.title: mbedTLS Renegotiation Vulnerability — Patch in Progress
security_advisories.summary: A TLS renegotiation vulnerability in the 4G LTE communication module has been identified. RailSecure is coordinating with infrastructure providers and is developing a patch. Interim mitigations are available.
security_advisories.workaround: Configure 4G network equipment to enforce TLS 1.3 at the infrastructure level. Disable renegotiation at the RBC gateway. Contact RailSecure support for detailed configuration guidance.
security_advisories.remediation_steps: Await patch 3.2.1 expected Q3 2026. Apply interim configuration changes to radio block centre gateway as per Technical Bulletin TB-2025-017.

security_updates.title: 3.2.0-P1: Crypto Library Update and Radio Hardening
security_updates.description: Updates mbedTLS from 2.28.0 to 3.1.0. Adds HMAC integrity verification for all 4G data frames at application layer. Disables SSLv3 and TLS 1.0 at compile time. Includes minor fixes for ETCS message logging race condition identified in field telemetry.

sbom_records.notes: Generated during pre-release build audit. Includes new 4G LTE stack components. All components verified against NIST NVD and OSV databases on generation date.
SPDX format required by one operator for their internal toolchain. Subset of full component list — see CycloneDX SBOM for complete inventory.

risk_assessments.title: ETCS L2 Onboard Unit — Initial CRA Cybersecurity Risk Assessment
risk_assessments.methodology: IEC 62443-3-2 Security Risk Assessment combined with EN 50159 safety and security threat analysis (TARA). Attack surface enumeration per ETCS communication profiles. Threat actor modelling aligned with ENISA Railway Cybersecurity Guidelines 2020.
risk_assessments.summary: Comprehensive TARA conducted for initial market release covering all external interfaces: GSM-R radio link, Eurobalise interface, STM host bus, and diagnostic port. Four critical and three high-severity threats identified. All critical threats mitigated to residual LOW prior to release. GSM-R authentication identified as the highest residual risk requiring ongoing monitoring.

risk_items.title: Rogue GSM-R Base Station — Forged Movement Authority
risk_items.description: An adversary operates a rogue GSM-R base station or compromises a legitimate RBC to inject forged movement authority telegrams, causing the onboard unit to authorise unsafe train movements or emergency stops at wrong locations.
risk_items.threat_scenario: Nation-state or sophisticated criminal actor deploys software-defined radio equipment near a railway line to impersonate a Radio Block Centre. Forged MA telegrams are transmitted during a time window when the legitimate RBC signal is weaker.
risk_items.asset_affected: GSM-R radio interface, Movement Authority processing module
risk_items.mitigation_plan: 1. Deploy HMAC-SHA256 session authentication (implemented in firmware). 2. Implement RBC identity certificate pinning. 3. Require operator infrastructure to use frequency monitoring equipment. 4. Add anomaly detection for unusual MA patterns in train management system.

risk_items.title: Malicious Eurobalise — Exploit via Malformed Telegram
risk_items.description: A physically replaced or tampered Eurobalise transponder in the track transmits malformed telegrams designed to exploit parsing vulnerabilities in the onboard unit, triggering undefined behaviour in the safety-critical supervision software.
risk_items.threat_scenario: An insider threat or physical attacker with track access swaps a legitimate balise for a modified device programmed to emit a crafted telegram. During a scheduled maintenance window, the adversary gains access to the track.
risk_items.asset_affected: Eurobalise telegram parser, SIL-4 supervision task
risk_items.mitigation_plan: 1. Implement strict bounds checking on all telegram fields (CVE-2021-31882 fix). 2. Use memory-safe parsing library with fuzz-testing validation. 3. Apply tamper-evident sealing on balise housings. 4. Regular infrastructure integrity inspections by maintenance teams.

risk_items.title: Diagnostic Port Exploitation via Maintenance Laptop Compromise
risk_items.description: A compromised or rogue maintenance laptop connected to the RS-232 diagnostic port during scheduled maintenance can issue firmware update commands without authentication, enabling firmware replacement with malicious code.
risk_items.threat_scenario: Supply chain attacker compromises the RS-DIAG diagnostic tool installer distributed via RailSecure's partner portal. Maintenance engineers unknowingly install the trojanised tool. During next maintenance session, the attacker's payload is executed with full firmware write access.
risk_items.asset_affected: RS-232 diagnostic interface, firmware update mechanism
risk_items.mitigation_plan: 1. Implement challenge-response authentication on diagnostic port using hardware security module. 2. Digitally sign all firmware update packages and verify signature before flash. 3. Distribute diagnostic tool via signed installer with code signing certificate. 4. Implement maintenance session logging with tamper-evident audit trail.

risk_items.title: STM Host Bus — Unauthorised Command Injection from STM Module
risk_items.description: A compromised Specific Transmission Module (STM) connected to the host bus could inject malformed messages into the ETCS host bus, potentially interfering with the core ETCS supervision logic.
risk_items.threat_scenario: Legacy national STM hardware has weaker security controls. A compromised STM (through supply chain or physical attack) sends crafted bus messages during operation.
risk_items.asset_affected: STM host bus interface, ETCS core supervision
risk_items.mitigation_plan: 1. Implement bus message origin validation. 2. Apply message rate limiting on STM bus. 3. Require STM modules to be from certified vendors. 4. Add bus traffic monitoring to detect anomalous patterns.

risk_assessments.title: ETCS L2 v3.2.0 — 4G LTE Interface Supplementary Risk Assessment
risk_assessments.methodology: Supplementary TARA focusing on new 4G LTE radio interface as a substantial modification per CRA Art. 3(4). Threat analysis per ETSI TS 133 501 (5G/LTE security architecture) and ENISA Telecom Security Guidelines. Attack surface delta analysis versus v3.1.0 baseline.
risk_assessments.summary: New 4G LTE interface introduces significant new attack surface compared to GSM-R baseline. Three new threats identified. Primary risk is TLS downgrade attack via renegotiation (CVE-2024-28869, currently in remediation). Residual risk for 4G interface assessed as MEDIUM pending patch 3.2.1. Infrastructure-level mitigations available and documented in operator technical bulletin.

risk_items.title: 4G LTE TLS Session Hijacking via Downgrade Attack
risk_items.description: The 4G LTE module's TLS implementation is susceptible to cipher suite downgrade attacks through renegotiation manipulation, potentially allowing an on-path attacker to decrypt ETCS application-layer traffic.
risk_items.threat_scenario: A sophisticated attacker with access to mobile network infrastructure (e.g., a compromised MVNO, rogue cell, or nation-state operator) performs a man-in-the-middle TLS renegotiation attack during an active ETCS session, downgrading cipher negotiation to a broken suite.
risk_items.asset_affected: 4G LTE communication module, ETCS application data confidentiality and integrity
risk_items.mitigation_plan: 1. Update mbedTLS to 3.4.0+ with renegotiation disabled (patch 3.2.1). 2. Enforce TLS 1.3 only at application layer. 3. Implement application-level message authentication independent of TLS. 4. Configure RBC gateways to enforce TLS 1.3 minimum. 5. Monitor for renegotiation events in network telemetry.

risk_items.title: 4G Network Outage — Loss of Movement Authority Communication
risk_items.description: 4G coverage gaps or network outages could cause loss of RBC communication in areas where GSM-R coverage is also degraded, triggering emergency brake application with safety implications for rail traffic flow.
risk_items.threat_scenario: Denial-of-service attack targeting 4G base stations in a specific rail corridor, or physical destruction of infrastructure, combined with existing GSM-R coverage gaps in tunnels.
risk_items.asset_affected: 4G LTE and GSM-R radio interfaces, train operational continuity
risk_items.mitigation_plan: 1. Implement automatic fallback from 4G to GSM-R with zero-latency handover. 2. Mandate operator coverage maps showing dual-coverage zones. 3. Emergency brake application on communication loss is the intended safe-state behaviour. 4. Deploy GSM-R repeaters in coverage gaps identified in field surveys.

cvd_policies.policy_text: RailSecure operates a coordinated vulnerability disclosure programme for all safety-critical railway products. Given the unique deployment environment of railway control systems — where patches require re-homologation and field installation by certified engineers — RailSecure requests an extended disclosure window of 120 days from initial report. During this period, RailSecure will: (1) acknowledge receipt within 5 business days, (2) provide a triage decision within 10 business days, (3) coordinate with affected infrastructure operators and National Safety Authorities, (4) develop and validate a patch meeting EN 50128 SIL requirements, (5) distribute the patch through certified field service channels. We work closely with ENISA and ERA on coordinated notification for cross-border rail impacts. We offer a bug bounty through our partner programme for valid reports. Please contact psirt@railsecure.de with PGP key ID 0xDEADBEEF.

support_periods.justification_text: Standard 5-year support period for initial release v3.1.0. Extended to account for railway homologation lead times — operators require minimum 18 months notice to plan migration due to NoBo re-certification requirements. End-of-support already reached; operators migrated to v3.2.0.
support_periods.expected_use_time_text: Railway onboard systems have typical operational life of 20-30 years. The software support cycle of 5 years reflects the cadence of baseline updates in ETCS Subset-026 and the homologation renewal cycle.
support_periods.comparable_products_text: Siemens Trainguard MT: 5-year software support + 10-year spare parts. Alstom Atlas: 7-year support for initial release. RailSecure aligns with industry standard.
support_periods.third_party_support_constraints_text: GSM-R network sunset planned by major EU operators 2028-2030. Security support constrained by availability of GSM-R network security updates from network vendors.
support_periods.user_facing_summary: Security updates for RailSecure ETCS L2 v3.1.0 were provided until 15 March 2024. Customers still operating v3.1.0 units should upgrade to v3.2.0 immediately.
support_periods.packaging_summary: Support end: 15 March 2024. Upgrade path available: v3.2.0.

support_periods.justification_text: 10-year extended support for v3.2.0 reflecting the operational lifespan of railway rolling stock. Extended period accounts for CRA Article 13(8) requirement to maintain security updates for the expected product lifetime and the exceptional lead times for railway patch deployment (typically 12-18 months from vulnerability discovery to fleet-wide deployment).
support_periods.expected_use_time_text: Railway rolling stock has operational life of 25-35 years. The v3.2.0 onboard unit is expected to serve until vehicle mid-life overhaul approximately 2035-2040 when a hardware platform upgrade will be conducted.
support_periods.comparable_products_text: Alstom Atlas ETCS: 10-year security support commitment. Bombardier INTERFLO 200: 8-year security support. RailSecure's 10-year commitment meets or exceeds industry standard.
support_periods.third_party_support_constraints_text: 4G LTE module longevity dependent on chipset vendor (Sierra Wireless HL8548G) support commitment through 2034. GSM-R alternative available for continuity. Network operator 5G migration plans being monitored.
support_periods.user_facing_summary: RailSecure provides security updates for v3.2.0 until 12 September 2032. Updates are delivered free of charge via certified field service or secure vendor download. Critical security patches are deployed with priority scheduling through your operator's maintenance programme.
support_periods.packaging_summary: Security support until: 12 September 2032. Updates: Free of charge via certified field service.

certification_records.scope_description: ETCS Onboard Unit v3.1.0 evaluation at EAL4 augmented with ALC_FLR.2 and AVA_VAN.5. Security Target covers GSM-R radio interface authentication, Eurobalise telegram parsing, and firmware integrity protection. Evaluation conducted per BSI Certification Scheme.
certification_records.notes: Renewed for v3.2.0 — see cert 0002. Expired certificate remains on file as evidence of evaluation at time of initial market placement.

certification_records.scope_description: ETCS Onboard Unit v3.2.0 evaluation at EAL4 augmented with ALC_FLR.3 and AVA_VAN.5. Security Target extended to cover 4G LTE interface and Subset-026 v3.6.0 protocol implementation. Delta evaluation against BSI-DSZ-CC-1123-2019 baseline.
certification_records.notes: Delta evaluation confirmed coverage of all new attack surfaces introduced by 4G LTE interface. Maintenance report MR-2023-001 confirms patch 3.2.0-P1 does not affect certification scope.

certification_records.scope_description: IEC 62443-4-2 Component Security Level 3 assessment for the ETCS Onboard Unit v3.2.0. Covers embedded system security requirements: identification and authentication, use control, system integrity, data confidentiality, restricted data flow, timely response to events, and resource availability.
certification_records.notes: Recertification in progress for v3.2.0 post-patch release. Interim compliance maintained via maintenance process per IEC 62443-4-2 clause 6.
